text:
alex.g: :rotating_light: getting paged — sudden bot-like spike hitting /v1/embeddings from multiple proxies, token-in rate ~18x baseline. users seeing 503s and long tail latencies.
oncall-bot: Paging oncall @sam.k (pg: embeddings-high-rate) — severity: high — pager sent.
sam.k: I'm up, looking now. do we have a source IP set?
priya: telemetry shows ~1200 unique src IPs in last 2m, but mostly same UA pattern: `python-requests/2.x` + header fingerprint. likely a scraper farm rather than legit customers.
security-bot: preliminary WAF signal: suspicious header signatures + repetitive payloads. recommending adaptive challenge on edge for suspicious fingerprints.
sam.k: ok start with soft measures — enable per-API-key rate-tiering and short circuit for anonymous keys. priya, can you identify top offending keys?
priya: listing now. top 3 keys account for 54% of requests but each looks like rotated proxies, suspect compromised or abused keys. sending list in DM.
alex.g: priority: avoid bringing down good customers. plan: 1) apply dynamic quota cap on embeddings route for unverified keys; 2) enable 403->429 transformation for repeat offenders; 3) edge WAF rule to challenge the header fingerprint; 4) disable batched async embeddings temporarily if pressure persists.
sam.k: on it — applying rate-tier policy `embeds_dynamic_2026-03-17` to rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100% to monitor impact. starting 10% canary now.
ops-lead: FYI I'll prepare a customer impact slice for status page. need quick numbers on affected tenants.
priya: canary at 10% applied to a subset of edge nodes in us-east-1. early telemetry: overall token-in rate dropped 12% in those nodes; tail latency unchanged globally (we're still seeing queuing elsewhere).
sam.k: expanding to 50% now. also adding extra token-bucket headroom for verified keys to avoid collateral.
security-bot: WAF challenge rule deployed in canary region. challenge rate ~0.6% of requests but blocks 22% of matched fingerprint traffic.
mia: customer-simulated traffic shows one major customer (acct: acme-ml) had 8% increase in error rate in the canary — routing them to verified-key path fixed errors. notifying account team.
alex.g: good catch — ops-lead, include acme-ml in the affected list; we should coordinate a short-term quota bump on their verified key if they need it.
ops-lead: noted. drafting status: "We are mitigating increased abusive traffic affecting embeddings. Some customers may see degraded performance while we apply protections. We're prioritizing verified customers."
sam.k: telemetry: after 50% rollout, global token-in decreased ~40%, error rate on embeddings dropped from 4.3% -> 1.1%. CPU on embed workers still elevated but stable.
priya: still seeing high fanout for async batch jobs — those amplify cost. propose disabling async batch ingestion for anonymous clients.
security-bot: recommending adding geo-stitching: throttle requests originating from known proxy ASN ranges.
sam.k: implemented anonymous batch disable and ASN-based throttle (~5k rpm cap per ASN). pushing now.
priya: immediate effect: async ingestion rate down 68%, cost-per-minute reduced. some small customers on dynamic IPs might be affected, adding notice.
mia: CX update sent to account team for acme-ml, they acknowledged — will monitor.
ops-lead: status page updated with initial mitigation note and we promised a follow-up at +30m with impact metrics.
alex.g: schedule: hold current mitigations for 1 hour then reassess. if bot adapts, escalate to hard WAF block list + temporary endpoint disable for highest-churn keys.
sam.k: agree. also enabling extra scrubbing on logs to surface any credential-stuffing patterns; run quick query for repeated failed auths in same time window.
security-bot: found suspicious auth attempts — ~200k failed token refresh attempts correlated with the spike. marking as credential-stuffing suspicion.
priya: cross-ref'd keys: many are rotated, likely botnet using token-refresh cycle. recommend rotating compromised keys and sending rotation notices to customers flagged as compromised.
alex.g: ops — prepare email templates and key-rotation flow for flagged tenants. include steps to rotate and request support if they see impact.
mia: preparing customer outreach for impacted verified customers only. non-verified will get a generic post-incident note.
sam.k: current snapshot (T+22m): token-in rate at 34% of peak, embedding error rate 0.9%, queue depth normalized by 20%. ready to hold mitigations and observe.
ops-lead: collecting final metrics for the 30m update. any objections to keeping ASN throttle and anonymous batch disable for 24h?
priya: thumbs up from infra — it's low risk and reduces blast radius.
security-bot: no objections; WAF challenge remains enabled for the next 24h, escalate to block if pattern recurs.
alex.g: ok locking in mitigations for 24h. follow-up: rotate compromised keys, notify affected customers, run postmortem on detection lag and refine fingerprint rules.
sam.k: will hand off to morning shift with runbook: steps to rollback, metrics to watch, and how to escalate to infra-sev if embeddings workers show >85% CPU or error rate >2.5%.
ops-lead: handing off to @sam.k for steady-state monitoring, I'll update incident channel at +30m.
mia: thanks team.
(oncall-bot): Incident status: mitigations in place, severity: reduced -> monitor.
